body.statement: Suppose \(K=4\) and \(m_*\le1/4\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), the response-type masses in \(\text{def:k4-legal-array}\) are nonnegative, sum to one in each covariate cell, satisfy conditional instrument independence, treatment and selected-outcome consistency, global no-defiers, increasing weak selection monotonicity, fair-instrument overlap, and the aggregate mass floor; hence \(Q_n^{(4)}\in\mathcal M\) and the displayed table is exactly \(p_n^{(4)}\). Its unconditional capacities are \(H_0=(1-r_n)(\ell^0,h^0)\) and \(H_1=r_n(\ell^1,h^1)\). The emerging-cell upper cuts are exactly \((.40,.30,.30,.40)\), so two cuts bind simultaneously; its lower and upper benefit masses are \(0\) and \(.30\), while the main-cell masses are \(0\) and \(.20\). The table contains the selected outcome atom \(p_n^{(4)}(0,0;0,1,0)=\lambda_{\mathrm r}/n\), and \[M(p_n^{(4)})=.25+.25r_n,\qquad \Phi(p_n^{(4)})=\left(0,\frac{.8+.4r_n}{1+r_n}\right).\] For either \(a_n=n^{-1/3}\) or \(a_n=n^{-0.49}\), the specific-array legal envelope has \(c_n\to_P\sqrt{1.28}z_{1-\alpha/2}\), the fallback probability tends to zero, \(P_n\{\Phi(p_n^{(4)})\in C_n\}\to1-\alpha\), and \[\sqrt n\{U(\widehat p_n)-U(p_n^{(4)})\}\Rightarrow N(0,1.28).\] The variance follows from the limiting main-cell ratio: its numerator event has probability \(.10\), its denominator event has probability \(.125\), and \(\{.10(.2)^2+.025(.8)^2\}/.125^2=1.28\); the emerging cell contributes deterministic root-\(n\) drift but only \(o_P(1)\) centered root-\(n\) noise.
body.justification: The proposition is a fully reproducible destructive check in the smallest array containing a rare observed atom, root-\(n\) support emergence, simultaneous cuts, and a degenerate lower endpoint.
body.gap: No cited paper verifies common-Gaussian legal-face calibration on a survivor-complier array combining an order-\(n^{-1}\) observed atom, order-\(n^{-1/2}\) support emergence, simultaneous ties, and a degenerate endpoint.
body.consumer: A certified legal-face implementation gains an exact atom-level regression test before attempting the full uniform theorem.
